title: AI Annotation Platform Product Management
subtitle: Walk into a director-level PM interview sounding like you built the annotation engine behind frontier AI models

modules.title: From Data Labeling to AI Data Production
modules.description: Understand how annotation has evolved from simple bounding boxes to expert feedback loops that shape frontier models. Learn the modern taxonomy of work: RLHF, red teaming, model evals, and constitutional AI.

topics.title: The shift from high-volume labeling to expert human feedback
RLHF workflows: preference ranking, comparison, and reward modeling
Red teaming, adversarial testing, and model evaluation tasks
Task taxonomy: classification, segmentation, transcription, rating, ranking, chain-of-thought, critique

modules.title: The Four Product Surfaces
modules.description: Map the platform's four distinct user personas — requester/customer, reviewer/expert annotator, ops/workflow manager, and platform/admin — and how their needs conflict and align.

topics.title: Requester/customer surface: dataset creation, project setup, quality SLAs, and data delivery
Reviewer/expert surface: task interfaces, instructions, payment transparency, and cognitive load
Ops surface: workforce routing, quality monitoring, adjudication queues, and throughput management
Platform/admin surface: ontology management, versioning, audit logs, and compliance

modules.title: Competitive Landscape and Strategic Wedges
modules.description: Analyze the major players (Scale AI, Labelbox, Snorkel AI, Surge AI, Mercor, SuperAnnotate) by their go-to-market wedges, platform differentiation, and where they win or lose.

topics.title: Scale AI: full-stack managed service, government/defense, and the API-first platform
Labelbox (tooling + marketplace) vs. Snorkel AI (programmatic labeling, weak supervision)
Surge AI, Mercor, SuperAnnotate: expert-first, niche vertical, and self-serve wedges
Build vs. buy decision factors: why Meta, OpenAI, and Anthropic build internal tools

modules.title: Quality Systems and Labeler Performance
modules.description: Design quality control mechanisms that catch errors early and improve over time: gold sets, consensus, calibration sessions, rubrics, and adjudication workflows.

topics.title: Task design and rubrics: reducing ambiguity and anchoring judgment
Gold sets, consensus labels, and inter-annotator agreement (IAA)
Calibration sessions, spot-checking, and adjudication queues
Diagnosing labeler quality problems: fraud, fatigue, misunderstanding, edge cases
Feedback loops: showing labelers their accuracy and teaching through rejection reasons

modules.title: Metric Trees for AI Data Platforms
modules.description: Build a metric tree that balances speed, quality, and model impact. Move beyond label volume to accepted data, downstream model performance, and customer retention.

topics.title: Choosing the north star: accepted high-quality data vs. raw label volume
Input metrics: task clarity, labeler training completion, gold set pass rate
Output metrics: precision/recall, IAA, rejection rate, time-to-delivery
Model impact metrics: uplift in eval benchmarks, human preference win rate, safety incidents

modules.title: Interview Execution and Question Design
modules.description: Prepare for common PM interview questions (product design, metrics, trade-offs, prioritization) and learn how to ask sharp questions back that signal deep platform thinking.

topics.title: Answering product design questions: 'Design a task interface for constitutional AI feedback'
Metrics and trade-off questions: 'How would you balance throughput vs. quality?'
Prioritization scenarios: roadmap for expert marketplace vs. self-serve tooling
Sharp questions to ask back: platform architecture, quality philosophy, build vs. vendor strategy
